# Finding families

Every graded finding carries a stable, dotted `family.item` code (charter koan 9, *errors are lore*). Clients and repair tools match on the code, which is stable across message wording. This page catalogues every code the system emits: its family (the check or tool that raises it), its severity, any structured repair it carries, and what it means.

These finding codes are **disjoint** from the wire error-code registry (the `ErrorCode` values in `error-codes.md`, per the dli-worker contract §3.2 / §9). The distinction is load-bearing: a wire error code says the *call* failed — it was malformed (`schema`), refused by principle (`refused`), or hit a server defect (`internal`); a finding code is a graded *domain* observation about the lore itself. A well-formed call over inconsistent lore returns findings, not an error. No code appears in both sets.

**93 dotted codes** across **11 families**, plus **4 `proof.resource-violation` sub-codes**. A `family.item` code names its check battery in the family and the specific violation in the item. Two codes can share a stem across families — the naming vet's `name.register-fit` (a kernel error) and the authoring seam's `name.unvetted` (an authoring warn) are different findings from different surfaces.


> Severity belongs to the emitting check. Some findings include structured repair data; others explain the next step in their message. Error-severity findings block `author.materialize`, while warnings do not.

## Entity references

- **Emitted by:** World check, CLI and authoring reads
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: check/entity.rs`
- **Severity:** Advisory; unknown references do not block a commit.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity.undeclared` | warn | `candidates` | a likely entity reference names no declared entity. |

## load — the loader's fail-closed gate

- **Emitted by:** the world loader, run by `deloreis check` / `dli.check` before any query
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: model.rs (LoadFinding)`
- **Severity:** All error: a load finding holds its declaration fail-closed — unassertable until fixed. Fail-closed provenance *is* the assertability gate.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load.missing-provenance` | error | — | a declaration carries no ruling and no hypothesis, so it cannot be asserted. |
| `load.malformed-provenance` | error | — | the provenance annotation cannot be read; held fail-closed until the annotation is fixed. |
| `load.malformed-world-rule` | error | — | a bare top-level world rule is not valid Datalog and is refused instead of lowering no rule. |
| `load.unbound-head-variable` | error | — | a rule concludes about a variable that nothing in its premises names. |
| `load.unknown-temporal-reference` | error | — | a typed temporal clause names an era or event the merged world does not declare. |
| `load.duplicate-declaration` | error | — | a name is declared twice as the same kind within one scope. |
| `load.cross-pack-collision` | error | — | a name is declared in more than one scope/pack. |
| `load.unstratifiable` | error | — | the rules cannot be ordered for evaluation — a negative-dependency cycle (FRONT-1). |
| `load.inert-declaration` | error | — | a declaration is accepted by the grammar but names nothing evaluable, so it would lower to no fact (DL-0029); surfaced rather than silently dropped. |

## predicate-identity — declared property-identity validation

- **Emitted by:** predicate-identity validation and policy projection in the world loader/check seam
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: model.rs (LoadFinding)`
- **Severity:** Mixed: an observed-shape mismatch is an error that blocks
            materialization; a union-policy promotion is a non-blocking warning.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `predicate-identity.arity-mismatch` | error | — | a certain predicate-identity component contains incompatible observed positional arities; materialization is refused rather than performing a partial merge. |

## continuity — the world-consistency battery

- **Emitted by:** world-internal and claim-relative continuity checks
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: check/continuity.rs (WorldFinding)`
- **Severity:** Errors block contradictions; warnings flag unresolved drafts or temporal gaps.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `continuity.chronology-cycle` | error | — | the before-graph closes a cycle; the timeline would have no consistent order. |
| `continuity.prior-contradiction` | error | — | a claim contradicts an established prior certain fact. |
| `continuity.rejected-lore` | error | — | a certain fact realizes a killed/rejected token. |
| `continuity.unknown-entity` | error | — | a claim references an entity that is not in scope. |
| `continuity.proposed-as-fact` | error | — | a claim states shadow (proposed) lore as settled. |
| `continuity.intra-episode-contradiction` | error | — | a claim set fixes one slot two contradictory ways within an episode. |
| `continuity.fluent-contradiction` | error | — | a fluent slot holds two distinct values certainly at once over overlapping intervals (a state's `since`/`until` spans collide). |
| `continuity.pending-conflict` | warn | — | a proposed value and another live value differ on a declared-functional non-fluent slot; the warning does not decide either account or block materialization. |
| `continuity.fd-violation` | error | — | canon's own certain layer holds two distinct values for a subject on a predicate the author declared `functional`, breaking the functional dependency. |
| `continuity.derived-fd-violation` | error | — | the same functional-dependency break as `continuity.fd-violation`, but visible only once the world's rules are saturated — a wire-authored rule (or an identity-closure copy) derives the second value rather than an author asserting it directly. |
| `continuity.identity-temporal-unsupported` | error | — | a `same-as` identity link names a declared era or event on either side — v1 refuses to unify time points (a defeasible merge over chronology indices would half-merge the timeline). |
| `continuity.fluent-order-undeclared` | warn | — | a fluent slot holds two distinct certain-support values whose temporal cover is undeclared-order-indeterminate at some point — a `before`-fact between the named anchors would settle whether they actually clash. Non-blocking: the contradiction check itself never fires on undeclared order. |
| `continuity.inertia-unanchored` | warn | — | a predicate declared `inertial` carries a value with no `since` anchor, so no forward-persistence interval can be derived — the declaration would silently do nothing. Non-blocking; names the slot so the missing anchor is a deliberate choice, not an accident (DL-0081, koan 4). |

## name — the naming-oracle kernel vet

- **Emitted by:** the world-true half of the naming oracle, run by `dli.name.check` and the language layer of `check`
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: language/derivation.rs (LangFinding)`
- **Severity:** Mixed: structural, register, uniqueness, morphology, and banned-token violations are errors; aural clashes, set clashes, sayability, and confusables are warnings. (Distinct from the authoring-seam `name.unvetted` finding below.)

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name.slot-sequence` | error | — | the name's slots match no name-kind pattern of its dialect. |
| `name.role-membership` | error | — | a name-part is not declared in the dialect under the role it fills. |
| `name.register-fit` | error | — | the name does not fit its declared dialect/register. |
| `name.phonotactics` | error | — | the name violates the dialect's phonotactics (vowels, endings, clusters, stress). |
| `name.uniqueness` | error | — | the name collides with an existing name in canon. |
| `name.fixed-token-reuse` | error | — | the name reuses a fixed token reserved elsewhere. |
| `name.aural-clash` | warn | — | the name is aurally too close to another across the whole name-space. |
| `name.set-clash` | warn | — | the name is not aurally distinct within its declared set. |
| `name.gender-morphology` | error | — | the name's morphology conflicts with its declared gender. |
| `name.sayability-cap` | warn | — | the name exceeds the configured sayability-tier caps. |
| `name.banned-in-name` | error | — | the name realizes banned diegetic vocabulary. |
| `name.confusable` | warn | — | the id mixes a Latin-looking form with a look-alike character from another script (a homoglyph). |

## attest — the attestation seam

- **Emitted by:** the attestation lookup a check consumes, surfaced by `dli.check` and `dli.attest.missing`
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: attest.rs (storage seam); dli-serve :: contract.rs + handlers.rs (document verdict)`
- **Severity:** Missing, stale, and negative judgments are errors for the consuming check; a current affirmative judgment is a pass with no severity.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attest.missing` | error | — | the question has no attestation in the store; a sweep must pose it before a check can consume it. |
| `attest.stale` | error | — | the stored judgment no longer matches the current world fingerprint. |
| `attest.pass` | — | — | the current bounded model judgment affirms the configured proposition at grade attested. |
| `attest.fail` | error | — | the current bounded model judgment rejects the configured proposition at grade attested. |

## practice — practice well-formedness

- **Emitted by:** the practice-block checker, run by `deloreis check` / `dli.check` when a `practice` is declared
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: practice.rs (PracticeFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error: a malformed practice cannot host a proof, so each finding blocks the practice.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `practice.error-refines-nothing` | error | — | a declared error refines a token that is not one of the seven structural classes L1–L7. |
| `practice.missing-discriminant` | error | — | two errors share a structural class with no discriminant to tell them apart. |
| `practice.resource-outside-algebra` | error | — | a resource's declared law is outside the closed resource algebra. |
| `practice.unbound-sort` | error | — | a role is typed by a sort the practice does not declare, that is not a primitive kind or an in-scope cycle. |
| `practice.unresolved-cycle` | error | — | a failure or law cites a cycle that is not in scope. |
| `practice.error-resource-unknown` | error | — | an L6 resource-violation error spends against a resource the practice does not declare. |
| `practice.renamed-interior-form` | error | — | a practice interior wrote a retired spelling (a killed form); refused with its successor named. |

## proof — the diegetic proof checker

- **Emitted by:** the proof/ledger checker, run by `deloreis check-proof` / `dli.check-proof`
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: ledger_check.rs (ProofFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error: a proof finding means the diegetic proof is invalid; the L-class in the message (L1–L7) names which structural obligation broke.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proof.unknown-form` | error | — | the form is not declared by this practice (L1). |
| `proof.premise-absent` | error | — | a premise is not established in the scene — the casting fizzles (L2, absent). |
| `proof.premise-contradicted` | error | — | a premise is denied by the certain projection — the casting rebounds (L2, contradicted). |
| `proof.wrong-phase` | error | — | a step runs at the wrong cyclic phase (L3, timing). |
| `proof.bad-instantiation` | error | — | a form is instantiated with ill-typed arguments (L4). |
| `proof.unknown-role` | error | — | the proof header binds a role the practice does not declare. |
| `proof.invalid-chain` | error | — | a chain step does not follow from its cited premises (L5). |
| `proof.resource-violation` | error | — | the ledger breaches a resource law (L6) — see the resource sub-codes below. |
| `proof.close-mismatch` | error | — | the close atom does not match what the steps derived (L7). |
| `proof.expectation-unmet` | error | — | the proof's expected verdict was not met (the expected-verdict discipline). |
| `proof.invalid-spend` | error | — | a spend draws against a resource illegally. |
| `proof.unknown-spoke` | error | — | a step cites a spoke or label that the proof does not define. |
| `proof.unknown-expectation` | error | — | an expectation names something the practice does not define. |
| `proof.missing-close` | error | — | the proof has no close step. |
| `proof.practice-mismatch` | error | — | the proof's `in <practice>` clause does not match the practice being checked. |
| `proof.invalid-header-layout` | error | — | the direct proof AST header is not `<role> <actor> in <practice>`. |
| `proof.malformed-body` | error | — | captured proof clauses do not replay through the canonical parser. |
| `proof.invalid-close-layout` | error | — | the proof does not carry exactly one final close. |

## factcheck — payload claim standing

- **Emitted by:** claim-relative certain-layer checks and the authoring seam
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: check/factcheck.rs; dli-serve :: author/reads.rs + author/tools.rs`
- **Severity:** All error: supported claims are silent; only contradicted and unsupported claims emit findings.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `factcheck.contradicted` | error | — | the claim conflicts with certain or explicitly rejected lore. |

## resource — the discriminants of proof.resource-violation

- **Emitted by:** the resource-algebra accounting inside the proof checker; carried as the discriminant of `proof.resource-violation`
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: resource.rs (ResourceViolationCode)`
- **Severity:** Sub-codes, not standalone families: each names how a `proof.resource-violation` breached the closed algebra.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overspent` | error | — | a linear or affine balance fell below zero — a unit was spent that was never accounted. |
| `over-capacity` | error | — | an affine balance rose above its declared capacity. |
| `not-conserved` | error | — | a `linear conserved` multiset did not net to zero at the close — a step minted or burned it. |
| `wrong-direction` | error | — | a graded-monotone grade moved against its one declared direction. |

## citation — lowering findings

- **Emitted by:** the evaluator's lowering pass, surfaced through `check`
- **Owner:** `dli-eval :: world.rs (LowerFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error for the affected claim: lowering keeps checking the rest of the world, but forged authority fails that claim closed.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `citation.unknown-decision` | error | — | a claim cites a decision the corpus never declares; the claim is failed closed. |

## author — authoring-seam findings

- **Emitted by:** the `author.*` MCP tools (the authoring seam)
- **Owner:** `dli-serve :: author/tools.rs + author/reads.rs (Finding)`
- **Severity:** Per-code severity gates `author.materialize`: an `error` blocks it, a `warn` passes. These are the findings that carry structured machine repairs.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render.provenance-unrepresentable` | warn | — | the staged declaration has provenance the text renderer cannot preserve; its rendered line is omitted. |
| `name.unvetted` | warn | `run-check` | a name has not passed the naming oracle; it enters proposed and unvetted. |
| `entity.unknown` | error | `resolve-entity` | no entity of that id is in scope; the claim is staged but cannot materialize until it exists. |
| `event.era-missing` | error | — | an event has no era anchor; every event must occur during a declared era. |
| `event.era-kind` | error | — | an event's era anchor names an entity that is not an era. |
| `fact.contradiction` | error | — | a claimed slot value contradicts a certain fact the base asserts. |
| `order.cycle` | error | — | a `before` fact would close a cycle against the existing orderings. |
| `consequence.changed` | warn | — | under a supposition the derived-consequence set may move; see `author.diff`. |
| `hypothesis.not-in-fork` | error | — | a hypothesis is legal only in a fork workspace. |
| `hypothesis.bundle-limit` | error | — | a proposal bundle carries at most one hypothesis; a second supposition is a second fork. |
| `hypothesis.unknown` | error | — | no hypothesis of that id is staged in this workspace to suppose. |
| `question.unknown` | error | — | no open question of that id exists in this workspace to add an option to. |
| `field.control-char` | error | `remove-control-chars` | a free-text field carries a control/bidi/zero-width character that could forge or reorder a declaration in the review diff. |
| `citation.unknown-decision` | error | `resolve-citation` | a cited decision id does not resolve against the decisions the corpus declares. The engine records the attribution a caller supplies but verifies that what it cites exists: the unknown decision's variable is left open, so the claim can never read certain, and materialize is barred until the id is repaired. |
| `decision.duplicate-in-batch` | error | — | one bulk decision-recording request repeats an exact decision id; the complete batch is refused atomically and the finding identifies both record positions. |
| `identity.self-merge` | warn | — | a `same-as` claim names the same id on both sides; it is a no-op merge. |
| `predicate-identity.self-merge` | warn | — | a predicate-identity claim names the same predicate on both sides; it is retained for provenance but has no semantic effect. |
| `identity.temporal-unsupported` | error | — | a `same-as` claim names an era or event endpoint; identity merging is not defined over the temporal spine (v1 boundary). |
| `identity.sort-mismatch` | warn | — | a `same-as` claim merges entities of different sorts (e.g. a person and a place); staged but flagged for review. |
| `rule.empty-body` | error | `add-body-literal` | a rule's body has no literals; a body-less rule would derive its head unconditionally on the wire, but its render reparses via the `.dli` text path to a malformed rule the loader refuses (migration parity). Refused before staging. |
| `rule.unbound-variable` | error | `bind-variable` | a rule's head, or a negated body literal, names a variable no positive body atom binds — a range-restriction (datalog safety) violation. Refused before staging. |
| `rule.duplicate` | error | — | a rule of that name is already staged or already in the compiled base; rule names are unique so `author.defeat` can cite one unambiguously. Refused before staging. |
| `rule.unstratifiable` | error | — | staging this rule alongside everything already staged would leave the world unstratifiable (a negative-dependency cycle); the stratification pre-flight refuses it before it ever reaches the workspace, so no add can brick a later read. |
| `state.anchor-kind` | error | `resolve-anchor` | a state's temporal anchor names a KNOWN entity of the wrong sort — `since`/`until` need an event, `after`/`during` need an era. |
| `workspace.base-missing` | error | — | the workspace's project document base is no longer loaded. |
| `world.uncompilable` | error | — | the staged declarations do not compile into a checkable world. |
